svg.title: Figure 4. Large deflection of a cantilever (the elastica)
svg.desc: Two panels. (a) The deflected shape of a cantilever with a vertical tip load for load parameters alpha of 0.5, 1.5, 3 and 6, drawn to equal scales: solid curves are the exact large-deflection shape, which keeps the strip's length so the tip swings inward, and dotted curves are linear theory, which keeps every point at its original x and runs far below the exact curves at the larger loads. (b) The vertical tip deflection over L and the inward tip movement over L against alpha: the vertical deflection follows the linear-theory line alpha over 3 at first and then bends over, approaching L slowly; a shaded band marks loads above about alpha = 0.68, where linear theory overstates the deflection by more than 5 percent.
